paras: The mob hunt for Huffman was a threatened lynching near Tiffin, Ohio, in October 1888, when a mob of men searched for a man named Huffman, accused of assaulting a six-year-old girl, with the stated intent of lynching him. The only reports are one wire dispatch, and none says whether he was caught.

According to a dispatch from Tiffin dated October 15, Huffman, described as about twenty years old, was accused of twice forcibly assaulting a six-year-old daughter of Frank Wise, who lived near the city limits, that day. The girl's mother was said to have caught him in the act the second time, but he escaped. The dispatch closed by saying that "a mob of men are hunting him" and that he would be lynched if found.
No report of his capture, arrest, trial or lynching appears in the coverage, and no paper gives his race or first name.

The St. Paul Daily Globe printed the story on October 16 as a special under the headline "Should Be Strung Up," calling Huffman a "lecherous villain." The same text ran the same day in the Beatrice Daily Express in Nebraska and on October 17 in the Yankton Press and Daily Dakotaian, both under the headline "There Is a Hell" and with "treacherous villain" in place of "lecherous." All three copies stated the accusation as fact and reported the mob's intent without comment.

The copies differ on the date: the St. Paul version is dated October 15 and places the assault "to-day," while the Yankton version is dated October 16 and gives no day; the earlier-printed St. Paul copy is the better guide.

accounts.label: Wire report from Tiffin
accounts.gist: Huffman twice forcibly assaulted Frank Wise's six-year-old daughter, was caught by her mother but escaped, and a mob was hunting him to lynch him.

framing.detail: The St. Paul Globe headed the dispatch 'Should Be Strung Up' and called Huffman a 'lecherous villain'.
The Yankton and Beatrice papers ran it as 'There Is a Hell', calling him a 'treacherous villain' and stating the accusation as fact.
